provenance.engineTransport: Node worker_threads with shared createPlannerSupervisor and canonical executePlanning

selection.rule: Among algorithms passing all selection seeds: highest mean fill, tie broken by lower mean horizontal CoG offset; evaluation seeds never used for selection.

definitions.fill: Total placed box volume / (pallet width × depth × allowed maximum height).
definitions.cog: Cargo mass-weighted geometric box centers; uniform mass within each box, product mass may differ; pallet mass excluded.
definitions.cogOffsetMm: Horizontal distance of cargo center of mass from pallet center; static balance proxy, not transport safety.
definitions.voidLiters: Pallet footprint × used height minus placed box volume; all unoccupied envelope space, NOT trapped/inaccessible void.
definitions.columnVoidLiters: Exact axis-aligned volume below the highest box top in each horizontal footprint column minus box volume; excludes air above local tops. Not a connectivity/robot-access/trapped-void proof.
definitions.minSupport: Minimum recorded supported-area ratio over placed boxes.
definitions.maxLoadRatio: Maximum loadAbove/effectiveMaxLoadKg from shared physical model; null if capacity is unknown.
definitions.uncertainty: Student t 95% CI over independent arrival seeds; unadjusted exploratory intervals, not universal algorithm ranking.
definitions.pareto: Descriptive nondomination of eligible held-out means: maximize fill, minimize horizontal CoG offset and CoG height. Uncertainty is shown separately; no arbitrary aggregate score.
definitions.voidCaution: A shallow, sparsely loaded pallet can have less envelope void simply because its used height is lower; compare together with fill/count. A low void value alone is not better packing.

assumptions: New sequential executions in the same shared engine; no previous experiment rows reused.
Synthetic 72-box input: 12 per SKU × 6 SKUs; maximum cargo height 1200 mm; one pallet; temporary buffer 0.
Robot cycle targets 10 and 12 seconds are assumed operating targets, not measured robot cycle times.
Recognition delay 0 seconds and validation/communication reserve 1 second are assumptions: available planner windows 9000 and 11000 ms.
Heavy-over-light ordering prohibition excluded by mentor agreement; support, allowable top load and robot proxy checks remain active.

Same shared candidate-search configuration and physical validation; algorithms may search/rank candidates differently. MCTS models future sequences from remaining counts, not actual future arrival order.
Warm-up is a separate 6-box trial per algorithm and is excluded from benchmark rows.
Single shared machine; wall-clock timings include scheduler effects. These are not CPU-time or real-robot sensing/IK measurements.
Planner elapsed and worker dispatch elapsed are preserved separately; worker startup is excluded by the shared supervisor.
A watchdog can stop search at 9/11 seconds and still deliver an earlier validated incumbent within the 10/12-second full cycle. Search termination is recorded separately from cycle deadline failure.
Confidence intervals use independent arrival seeds (n=5 evaluation), Student t; pairwise intervals are exploratory and not multiplicity-adjusted.
Static CoG and envelope void are descriptive proxies, not experimentally validated transport stability or trapped void.
